issues.legal_issue: A claimed special form of marriage was not established by the evidence for purposes of family membership and property rights.
material_facts: The claimants relied on a document recording that the marriage had been performed in the special form, but the family’s de facto manager and other senior members had not signed it.
The bride’s family had borrowed a substantial sum shortly before the marriage, and a substantial payment was made at the marriage.
Other family members denied that the couple were members of the family and dealt with family property without recognizing any interest of theirs.
The couple did not live in the family home except briefly, receive family income, or claim a share of it for many years.
The witnesses supporting the claim were related to the claimant, and the respectable attendees and the priest said to have officiated were not called to testify.
The party relying on the marriage’s special form had not attended the marriage and had taken inconsistent positions about it.
issues.conclusion: The evidence did not establish that the marriage was performed in the claimed special form, so the claimants could not rely on it to establish family membership or obtain relief in the family-property suits.
issues.legal_principle: Whether the claimed form of marriage was proved was determined from the evidence as a whole, including the circumstances surrounding the marriage, the document recording it, the parties’ subsequent conduct, and the quality of the oral evidence. The court did not apply or cite a statutory provision or an earlier case on this issue.

rule.if: civil_family_property_appeal and special_marriage_claimed_as_basis_for_family_rights and manager_did_not_sign_marriage_record and family_members_denied_claimants_membership and claimants_did_not_exercise_family_rights and supporting_testimony_lacked_independent_corroboration

predicates.civil_family_property_appeal: The proceeding is a civil appeal concerning claims to family membership or family property.
predicates.special_marriage_claimed_as_basis_for_fa: The claimants relied on a claimed special form of marriage to assert family membership or property rights.
predicates.manager_did_not_sign_marriage_record: The family’s person managing its affairs did not sign the document recording the claimed form of marriage.
predicates.family_members_denied_claimants_membersh: Other family members denied the claimants’ membership and dealt with family property without recognizing their interests.
predicates.claimants_did_not_exercise_family_rights: The claimants did not live as family members, receive family income, or claim a share of family property for a substantial period.
predicates.supporting_testimony_lacked_independent_: The supporting witnesses were interested or related, and available independent witnesses to the marriage were not called.

issues.definition: When claimants in a family-property appeal rely on a special marriage to establish family rights, the stated circumstances together mean that the special marriage is not established.

issues.legal_issue: A document that only records or confirms rights said to arise from a special marriage does not itself create those rights when the marriage and the claimed pre-existing rights are not established.
material_facts: The claimants relied on a later document from the last surviving family member as an alternative basis for their property claim.
That document described the claimants’ rights as arising from the special form of marriage and purported to confirm or release those asserted rights.
The court found that the special form of marriage had not been established and that the claimants therefore had no pre-existing rights of the kind described in the document.
An earlier settlement of the property in favour of another person had not been displaced.
issues.conclusion: The later document did not create an interest in the property for the claimants, and their alternative claim based on it failed.
issues.legal_principle: The effect of a document depends on what it says it does. A document that confirms or releases asserted pre-existing rights does not convey an interest where those rights did not exist; the court also held that the earlier settlement remained effective unless displaced. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this conclusion.

predicates.civil_family_property_appeal: The proceeding is a civil appeal concerning claims to family property.
predicates.claimants_rely_on_later_property_documen: The claimants rely on a later document as a basis for obtaining an interest in the property.
predicates.document_only_confirms_preexisting_claim: The document describes itself as confirming or releasing rights the claimants already allegedly possess, rather than independently granting them an interest.
predicates.claimed_preexisting_rights_not_establish: The claimants fail to establish the rights that the document says they already possess.
predicates.prior_property_settlement_not_displaced: An earlier settlement of the property remains effective and has not been set aside or otherwise displaced.

issues.definition: Where a later document only confirms claimed pre-existing rights, those rights are not established, and an earlier property settlement remains effective, the later document creates no property interest.
